title: Thermodynamics of Learning: A Typed Four-Component Accounting of Memory, Fit, and Value
abstract: What a finite learning device has recorded and what will hold value for it on future tasks are not the same quantity. We develop a typed accounting for finite-state learning devices that separates four components: a training-side fit functional $Φ_{\mathrm{fit}}$, the record-correlation stock $J_{D}=I(M;D)$, an update-side search ledger $σ_{M}$, and an operational capital value $V(M;T,b)$. This value is the work gap between an informed protocol class and a blind class obtained by deleting the memory-read port and re-optimizing from scratch. (I) Separation: for every $n$, there is a device family on which record correlation and world correlation grow by $n\ln 2$ while the capital gain is exactly zero. In the $\mathrm{flat}^{*}$ regime, data-free updates never increase $V$. (II) Capitalization ledger: an exact $\mathrm{flat}^{*}$ extraction identity and a universal ledger identity give, for (F5$'$)-stable $M$-local updates under a no-discarded-record-correlation condition (f), the bound $η_{\mathrm{cap}}\le 1$ for the capitalization efficiency $η_{\mathrm{cap}}=ΔV/(k T\,σ_{M})$, together with necessary and sufficient conditions for equality. (III) Value retention: for the retention gap $L_{\mathrm{gen}}$ and retention ratio $ρ_{\mathrm{gen}}$ (the former carries no sign constraint; the latter is defined for positive training-side value and is not confined to $[0,1]$) we give a two-layer alignment domain: an exact exchange rate between value and the side-information-adjusted record fit $I(M';D\mid Y)$ without any record-side-information independence assumption, and a raw record-stock exchange rate under a joint side-information neutrality condition $(M,D)\perp Y$, whose boundary is marked by an explicit one-time-pad witness. These are statements about finite-device value retention under task-distribution shift, not a theory of statistical generalization.
summary: This paper introduces a rigorous, four-component thermodynamic accounting system to quantify the difference between what is merely stored (memory) and what truly retains operational value in a learning device. By defining 'value' as an achievable work gap, it provides exact theorems governing how this value changes under task shifts or updates. It offers a powerful theoretical tool for analyzing information processing beyond standard generalization bounds.
main_problem: The paper develops a typed accounting framework to rigorously separate the physical quantity recorded by a finite-state learning device (memory) from the actual operational value that will persist or be useful for future tasks.
main_result: It establishes precise, non-trivial bounds and exchange rates governing how 'value' is retained or capitalized during task-distribution shifts, showing that simple measures like record correlation do not capture this full operational value.
method: The authors employ a novel four-component accounting system (fit functional, record-correlation stock, update ledger, and operational capital value) derived from information theory and thermodynamics principles.
model_or_system: The model is an abstract, finite-state learning device operating under defined protocols ($	ext{Protb}$), involving memory states ($M$), training records ($D$), and future task distributions ($T$). It analyzes the work gap between informed and blind protocol classes.
key_observables: Operational capital value $V(M; T, b)$, record-correlation stock $I(M; D)$, capitalization efficiency $\eta_{	ext{cap}}$, retention gap $L_{	ext{gen}}$, and the four component currencies ($C_1$ through $C_4$).
important_parameters: Budget ($b$), temperature ($kT$), memory size ($n$), and various functional parameters defining stability regimes (e.g., $\mathrm{flat}^{*}$ regime).
main_assumptions: The results are strictly limited to finite-state learning devices operating within a fixed, explicit operational framework; the paper explicitly states it is not a theory of statistical generalization.
figures_summary: Figures and tables define the four component currencies and illustrate theorems connecting these accounts, such as showing how different protocols yield distinct energy bounds ($\Delta V$).
paper_structure: The structure builds from defining the four-component accounting system to proving three main theorems: Separation (I), Capitalization Ledger (II), and Value Retention (III). The analysis uses specific computational witnesses (S, B, A) to derive these rigorous statements.
why_interesting: While abstract, the framework provides a deep thermodynamic analogy for information processing. Concepts like 'operational capital' and 'work gap' resonate with non-equilibrium statistical mechanics approaches used to study computation or energy dissipation in complex systems.
